text:
eli: Paging SRE oncall — we're seeing a sudden spike in 5xx from the gateway starting ~10m ago. Several streaming clients report 'stream closed' and chunked-encoding EOFs. @oncall-bot escalated.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2360004321 — Gateway 5xx surge affecting streaming responses. Severity: P1. Pager: eli.

maria: tl;dr customers on streaming endpoints get mid-stream disconnects + elevated 502/504. Non-streaming requests mostly succeed but with higher p50 latency. Noted region: us-west-2.

ash: observed same. Metrics: gateway 5xx rate jumped from ~0.1% -> 6% in 8m. Backend (runtime) error rates at 2.5%. Gateway logs show upstream timeouts and 'unexpected EOF' for chunked responses.

samir: copying logs snippet:```
[2026-03-15T10:23:41Z] gateway proxy: 502 -> upstream read: connection reset by peer; partial chunk sent
[2026-03-15T10:24:02Z] runtime: stream write error: write tcp 10.0.5.12:443: write: connection reset by peer
[2026-03-15T10:24:12Z] gateway: 504 -> upstream timeout waiting for body
```

jess: any deploys around that time?

eli: deploy-bot shows no full deploys in the last hour. A small canary rollout started ~30m ago but no config changes to streaming layer.

ash: hypothesis: intermittent NAT gateway / network flakiness causing upstream resets, or our continuous batching optimization is over-eager and causing partial chunk flush issues. Also seeing more client cancels.

maria: customer-impact: product-cs reported 3 mid-tier customers with ~10-30% of streaming requests failing. For some apps that relies on streaming (progressive responses) this is user-visible. Not yet a major revenue impact but urgent for SLA.

samir: quick mitigation options: 1) temporarily disable continuous batching for streaming routes; 2) increase upstream timeouts and retries at gateway; 3) route streaming traffic to older stable pool (fallback). Which is fastest?

eli: do 1) and 2) now. Ash, can you flip batching flag for streaming routes and push a timeout bump? Keep changes minimal. We'll consider route fallback if that doesn't move error rate within 5–10 minutes.

ash: on it. Pushing feature-flag change: `feature.streaming_continuous_batching=false` for prod gateway-pool.

ash: command I ran:```bash
curl -X POST "https://admin.internal/flags/streaming/continuous_batching" -d '{"enabled":false}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer **REDACTED**'
```

ash: also increased upstream read timeout from 15s -> 30s on streaming proxy config and reloaded.
deploy-bot: Config reload succeeded on 6/6 gateway instances.

samir: monitoring: watching 5xx and streaming disconnects. setting an alert window to 1m.

eli: notify CS: jess, product-cs, put interim note to impacted customers: "We are investigating intermittent streaming disconnects; mitigation in progress."

product-cs: messaging prepared and sent to affected customers with temporary workaround (switch to paged API if possible).

(5m pass)

ash: initial signal looks promising. Gateway 5xx down from 6% -> 1.1%, runtime errors still ~1.8% but trending down. Streaming client disconnect rate dropped ~60%.

maria: good. We should still run a deeper root-cause trace. Any correlation with particular model variants or request size?

samir: early traces show larger tokens-in-flight sessions (longer contexts) more likely to see resets. KV cache pressure correlated: hosts with high cache miss rates have more timeouts.

eli: next steps: keep mitigation live for now. Do a controlled rollback of the canary to confirm independence. Also spin up a dedicated lane for streaming to isolate from paging workloads.

ash: starting canary rollback to previous runtime image for the canary hosts. If that reduces runtime errors we can attribute it to the canary.

samir: in parallel I want to enable per-request streaming heartbeats from gateway to runtime (short no-op chunk every 10s) so proxies/TCP won't idle out. Can we enable as a feature flag? There is a small perf cost but useful for stability.

eli: yes, but only after we confirm batching toggle is the main fix. If errors bounce back we'll enable heartbeat and consider sticky connections for long streams.

(10m pass)

ash: canary rollback started; redeploying previous image to 3 canary hosts.

deploy-bot: Canary rollback staged. 3/3 canary hosts reverted.

samir: post-rollback metrics: runtime errors down to 0.6%. Looks like the canary contributed to instability. Interesting: the canary included a micro-optimization in the gRPC streaming flush logic.

eli: that aligns with continuous-batching hypothesis. Outcome: root cause likely a combination of (a) a canary change that altered flush semantics in streaming codepath and (b) some hosts under KV pressure increased latency causing upstream timeouts and resets.

maria: customer impact update: affected customers verified restored service after our mitigation and rollback. Confirmed for two large customers. One smaller still sees intermittent cancels — investigating if they use extremely long contexts.

jess: what's the plan for follow-up?

eli: action items: 1) samir to open INC-2360004321-RCA with timeline and trace evidence (incl logs above). 2) ash to re-enable continuous batching only after canary validates changes and rollback fix is merged to canary RC. 3) engineering to add streaming-heartbeat flag and test. 4) product-cs to follow up with customers and offer fallback to paged endpoints. 5) set postmortem meeting tomorrow.

samir: I'll include traceback of the flush change and heap/kvcache metrics. Also propose a probe to emulate long-lived streams under KV pressure for future testing.

ash: will add e2e test for streaming flush semantics and add a safeguard feature flag on gRPC flush behavior.

eli: thanks everyone. Lowering page. Keep monitoring for 30m and escalate if errors >1.5%.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-2360004321: status -> mitigation in progress. Severity -> reduced to P2 pending RCA.

product-cs: closing customer notices after confirmation from 3/4 impacted that service stabilized. Remaining customer support ticket assigned to jess.

eli: tl;dr summary to paste into RCA: brief spike in gateway 5xx/timeouts causing streaming disconnects driven by an unsafe canary change to streaming flush behavior + KV pressure on a subset of hosts. Mitigations: disabled continuous batching for streaming, increased upstream timeouts, rolled back canary, reloaded gateway config. Recovery observed within ~12 minutes of mitigation sequence.

samir: filing RCA now. I'll include recommended follow-ups: improved canary gates for streaming, heartbeat option, load probes for long-lived streams, and customer-facing guidance to use paged endpoints where appropriate.

eli: good job. Stand down unless any regression.
